source.label: Placed in NGC 300 as the app draws it, where the star's sight line crosses the disc's midplane: 2,086,765 pc (src/objects/ngc-300-layers/source/recipe.json: centre 2,089,296 pc, inclination 44 deg, line of nodes 110 deg). The galaxy's distance, which places the galaxy and not a star within it: Tully2009AJ....138..323T: The Extragalactic Distance Database (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009AJ....138..323T); catalogue reference Tully2009AJ....138..323T: 2089296.13085 pc (-56939.1199178/+58534.3432765); trgb

controls.label: Color
controls.qualification: Color of a blackbody at the star's temperature; darkening toward the edge from a model atmosphere. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The color of a blackbody at the star's published temperature. The darkening toward the edge is the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 4,780 K and log g 0.65 (u1 0.689, u2 0.088): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The spin axis's direction on the sky is a display convention.

physical.credit: Groenewegen radius; Gieren et al. (2004), AJ 128, 1167 position; cited distance; no measured rotation axis (display convention)
